title: Checkout UI and payment flow
idea: The payment frontend is one checkout screen driven by a reducer that sends each payment once, reuses its Idempotency-Key on retry, and polls until UPI settles.
points: `CheckoutPage` owns the reducer; the picker and pay button only dispatch events.
A network error keeps the key and locks the method; a decline starts fresh.
UPI returns PROCESSING; the screen polls a few times, then defers to the webhook.
Follow-ups: saved cards through gateway tokens, webhook load, and a ledger for reports.

edges.label: owns
edges.caption: CheckoutPage owns the reducer state. Children read props and dispatch events.
OrderSummary shows the items and the total, stored in minor units and formatted only for display.
MethodPicker collects a UPI id, or shows the gateway's card fields.

edges.label: card
edges.caption: In a typical design, card numbers go into gateway-hosted fields. Your page only receives a token.
The pay button dispatches PAY_CLICKED. The reducer ignores it unless the step allows paying.

edges.label: POST /payments
edges.caption: An effect sends one request per SUBMITTING step, with the reducer's Idempotency-Key.

edges.label: PROCESSING
edges.caption: For UPI the answer is PROCESSING. The poller asks again until SUCCEEDED, FAILED or the poll limit.

code.title: Checkout reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then replace the SUCCEEDED poll with two PROCESSING polls and predict the last step.

walk.text: The click handler makes the key. State: step, method, key, payment id, polls, error.
Changing method works only while choosing, and clears any old key.
Pay runs only from CHOOSING or RETRY. It keeps an existing key, else takes the event's.
A network error means unknown: keep the key, lock the method, offer retry.
SUCCEEDED ends the flow. FAILED is final: key and poll count reset for a new try.
PROCESSING waits for approval; after three polls the screen stops and defers to the webhook.

code.caption: A React component that renders state and runs effects. In the app, pay.mjs exports `reduce` and `initial`. Not run here.

walk.text: `useReducer` keeps all screen state in the reducer from pay.mjs.
Effect: one request per SUBMITTING step; a thrown fetch becomes NETWORK_ERROR.
Effect: while awaiting approval, poll every three seconds and clear the timer.
The method is locked unless the step is CHOOSING.
Errors render in an alert region so screen readers announce them.
The button is disabled while busy and sends a fresh key; the reducer ignores extras.

pitfalls: Disabling the button is not enough; the reducer and the key must also stop repeats.
Never let a card number reach your server; use the gateway's hosted fields.
Interview follow-up: replace polling with server push when many users wait on UPI.

quiz.q: In the run, which key does the retry after NETWORK_ERROR use?
quiz.why: NETWORK_ERROR keeps payKey because the first request may have charged. PAY_CLICKED takes the event's newKey only when payKey is empty.

takeaway: One reducer, one key per payment intent, and polling that knows when to stop.
